statuses.reason: The operation names no object, so ObjectNotFound has nothing to report. GET /user-defined-values and GET /webhooks take no parameters and no body. GET /communication-permissions/{permission_type} takes permission_type, an enum of channels (email, sms, phone) that request validation answers with 400, plus days and paging. The same rule as the top-level waiver for getTagsList and the other list operations.

requestBodies.Webhook names no existing object. Its id field is the webhook's own id, which a create cannot refer to, so the mock ignores it. name, url, authentication, auth_token and events are plain values. With nothing to look up, ObjectNotFound cannot be produced.

The path and body name no object. category_id on paths./templates.get is a list filter. The only documented behavior for an id filter naming no object is paths./debts.get debt_category_id: 'Another organisation's id matches nothing'. An unknown template category therefore returns an empty list, not 404.

Production answers 200 with an empty tags list for a user id that names no user (probe P7a), so getUsersTagsList never answers 404. The same rule as PARITY.md 'Ids that name no object': an id that matches nothing gives an empty list. addTagToUser and removeTagFromUser still answer 404 for an unknown user.
Production answers 200 with an empty permission_list for a value nobody has (probe P6b), so a lookup never answers 404. updateCommunicationPermissions still answers 404 when nothing matches.

properties.reason: Production's email lookup carries four keys (id, email, allow_comm_via_email, allow_comm_via_email_date) and no phone_slug (probe P6a). The mock gives sms and phone lookups the same four keys with phone, an inference, so phone_slug stays documented but is never emitted.
The changed-permissions list uses the same item shape as a lookup: four keys and no phone_slug (probe P6a, extended to sms and phone by inference). phone_slug stays documented but is never emitted.
